title: Silver in US soil and sediment: spatial declustering
source: USGS National Geochemical Database legacy soil and sediment best-value exports

national.origin: fixed projected (0,0) per component; 10 by 10 deterministic offsets
national.weight_rule: Each occupied cell across all included components receives equal mass per origin; fit averaged per-record weights

column_notes.mu: mean of log concentration in mg/kg
column_notes.n_positions: reported coordinate pairs, not certified sites
column_notes.kish_n: weight imbalance diagnostic, not independent spatial sample size

state.jurisdictions: 50 states and District of Columbia, separately for each medium
state.origin: per-case projected minimum extent; 10 by 10 offsets
state.projections: Per-medium, per-state WGS84 LAEA; center is coordinate medians of all bounded explicitly US metadata before Ag selection, rounded to 10 decimals
state.units: Concentration fields ending _mgkg are mg/kg; fractions are 0 to 1; pct_censored is percent

scope: Pooled recorded-method descriptive fits on occupied sampled support. No raw sample records included.
reproduction: The public standalone workflow implements these settings and is checked on synthetic inputs and independent numerical fixtures; archived aggregate results were not all refitted for this publication. Generated long-form estimates differ in layout from the curated wide state table.
limits: No harmonization of analytical methods, soil horizons or sediment types
Arithmetic model moments are exploratory and can fail high-tail checks
Missing or unavailable estimates remain NA, never zero or an automatic national fallback
